text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat reviewed the last points of dispute in a Hebron agreement with the Israelis.
- Damascus Declaration states said in the final statement of their meeting in Cairo that regional cooperation is subject to Israeli withdrawal from Arab territory.

- Mubarak will announce the start of the project to develop the south of the valley at the start of the new year. The irrigation canal will cost 5.5 billion pounds ($1.6 billion) and scientific studies have shown that the course is correct.
- Mubarak received the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Syria and Bahrain.
- Mubarak will meet Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri and the ministerial committee on the New Valley project this morning to discuss the final shape of the project.

- Th final statement of the Damascus Declaration meeting affirmed commitment to the resolutions of the Cairo summit. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said everyone must take our resolutions seriously. The meeting said the references for the Middle East peace process were the Madrid conference, U.N. resolutions and the principle of land for peace.
- The Christmas storm drowned Alexandria with rain.
- In 1997 seven million families will benefit from comprehensive social insurance.
- After his meeting with Mubarak, Arafat said: "we are trying to overcome the obstacles to agreement on Hebron."
- The ministerial commitee on the New Valley project discussed the civil works for the pumping station and the course of the irrigation canal.
- After the Damascus Declaration meeting, Moussa said the meetings were an excellent supplement to Arab action. Any arrangements in northern Iraq require Baghdad's approval.
- 30,000 tourists have come to Egypt in the past three days for the Christmas and New Year holidays.
